story.iWant: to place clips on multiple timeline tracks
story.soThat: I can create picture-in-picture or overlay effects
story.tasks: - Task 1: Extend timeline data model for multi-track support - Task 2: Create TimelineTrack component with visual track separation - Task 3: Update Timeline component to render 2 tracks - Task 4: Implement drag-and-drop to specific tracks - Task 5: Extend editing operations for track-aware behavior - Task 6: Implement multi-track preview compositing - Task 7: Update export pipeline for multi-track rendering - Task 8: Add visual indicators and track management UI - Task 9: Handle edge cases and error scenarios - Task 10: Testing and validation - Task 11: NFR Validation

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Timeline displays 2 horizontal tracks: Track 1 (main) and Track 2 (overlay) 2. Users can drag clips from media library to either track 3. Track 2 clips render on top of Track 1 in preview (overlay/PiP positioning) 4. Each track independently supports trim, split, delete operations 5. Playhead synchronizes across both tracks during playback 6. Export renders both tracks composited into single output video 7. Track 2 clips show visual indicator (border/label) distinguishing from Track 1

docs.doc: Defines Track interface (id, clips array, height), Clip interface with trackId field, TimelineState with tracks array, and multi-track actions: addClipToTrack(), getClipsForTrack(). PiP compositing uses Canvas API at 30fps per NFR003.
Workflow for drag-drop to tracks: highlight based on mouse Y position, call addClipToTrack(clip, trackId), prevent overlapping clips, clips stay within same track unless explicitly moved.
Canvas rendering loop via requestAnimationFrame: draw Track 1 full-size, draw Track 2 as overlay (25% size) in bottom-right corner, sync currentTime to playhead, 30fps requirement.
FFmpeg overlay filter for export: [1:v]scale=iw*0.25:ih*0.25[pip];[0:v][pip]overlay=W-w-10:H-h-10. Canvas fallback if FFmpeg fails. Audio mixed from both tracks.
Use Zustand for timelineStore extensions. Maintain immutability patterns for multi-track state updates.
Video.js for single-track playback (hardware accelerated), Canvas API for multi-track compositing overlay rendering.
Components in Timeline/ folder: Timeline.tsx, TimelineTrack.tsx, TimelineClip.tsx. Use PascalCase for components, camelCase for services/stores/types.

artifact.reason: Contains timeline state management. Must be extended with tracks array and multi-track actions (addClipToTrack, getClipsForTrack).
Main timeline component. Must be updated to render 2 TimelineTrack components stacked vertically, share ruler and playhead across tracks.
Individual clip rendering. Must preserve trackId during trim/split/delete operations.
Drag source for clips. Must be updated to support track-targeting during drag-drop.
FFmpeg export service. Must be extended with multi-track export method using overlay filter.

node.package: State management for multi-track timeline store
FFmpeg 6.0 for multi-track export with overlay filters

native.api: Track 1 and Track 2 video sources for Canvas compositing

story-context.constraints: - Multi-track state managed in Zustand timelineStore with immutability patterns (ADR-001) - Maximum 2 tracks: Track 1 (main, id=1), Track 2 (overlay, id=2) per ADR-010 - Clip interface must include trackId field (1 or 2) - Timeline must maintain single playhead synchronized across both tracks - Canvas compositing must maintain 30fps minimum during playback (NFR003) - Track 2 clips render as overlay/PiP in bottom-right corner at 25% size - FFmpeg overlay filter for export: [1:v]scale=iw*0.25:ih*0.25[pip];[0:v][pip]overlay=W-w-10:H-h-10 - Drag-drop must prevent cross-track movement unless explicitly intended - Prevent clip overlap on same track - All file paths stored as absolute paths - Use Tailwind CSS for styling (ADR-003), no separate CSS files - Use path.join for all file path operations - Component naming: PascalCase for components (Timeline.tsx), camelCase for stores (timelineStore.ts) - Visual indicators: Track 1 cyan border, Track 2 purple border for distinction (AC7)

tests.standards: Use Jest for unit testing (from electron-react-boilerplate). Unit tests for multi-track store operations (addClipToTrack, getClipsForTrack) with 95%+ coverage target. Manual integration testing for drag-drop, preview compositing, and export. Performance validation: 30fps with 10+ clips during playback (NFR001). Canvas compositing frame rate monitoring during preview.
tests.locations: src/renderer/src/store/__tests__/ Manual testing: timeline interactions, preview playback, export verification
tests.ideas: - AC1: Unit test Track interface and tracks array initialization (2 tracks) - AC2: Manual test drag clip from media library to Track 1, then Track 2, verify independent placement - AC3: Manual test preview playback with clips on both tracks, verify Track 2 renders as overlay in bottom-right - AC4: Unit test trim/split/delete operations preserve trackId, Manual verify operations work independently per track - AC5: Manual test playhead synchronization across both tracks during playback, scrubbing - AC6: Manual export multi-track timeline, verify output video has composited overlay using FFmpeg filter - AC7: Manual verify Track 2 clips show visual indicator (purple border, track label) - NFR001: Performance test with 10 clips (5 per track), verify 30fps during zoom, drag, playback - Edge case: Drop clip between tracks defaults to Track 1 - Edge case: Canvas compositing failure falls back to Track 1 only (no crash)
